title: Concept 7. Model Unavailability
summary: Model unavailability happens when the provider is operating, but the particular model you requested cannot be accessed.

sections.title: 1. What is model unavailability?
sections.body:
Model unavailability happens when the provider is operating, but the particular model you requested cannot be accessed.

This is different from a complete provider outage.

Example:

```text
Provider A = Available

Model X = Available
Model Y = Unavailable
Model Z = Available
```

Your application uses Model Y, so your requests fail even though the provider itself is healthy.

sections.title: 2. Why does it happen?
sections.body:
Common reasons:

- Incorrect model identifier.
- Model does not exist in the selected region.
- Model access has not been granted.
- Model is temporarily disabled.
- Deployment is unavailable.
- Account does not have model permissions.
- Model has been retired.
- Model capacity is unavailable.

sections.title: 3. Where does it happen?
sections.body:
- Model routing layer.
- LLM Gateway.
- Provider API.
- Cloud model deployment.
- Regional model deployment.

sections.title: 4. Real-time example
sections.body:
Your application uses:

```python
response = await acompletion(
    model="provider/model-x",
    messages=messages
)
```

But the provider no longer supports that model identifier.

The application receives an error such as:

```text
Model not found
Model unavailable
Deployment not found
```

The model may not be available in your account, deployment or region.

sections.body:

2. Provider model catalog.

4. Account permissions.
5. Provider error code and message.
6. Model lifecycle and retirement notices.

sections.title: 6. How to fix it?
sections.body:
### Solution 1 — Maintain model registry

Maintain an approved model configuration.

```python
MODEL_REGISTRY = {
    "fast": "provider/model-small",
    "reasoning": "provider/model-large",
    "backup": "provider/backup-model"
}
```

### Solution 2 — Model fallback

If the preferred model is unavailable, route to another approved model.

### Solution 3 — Model health checks

Periodically validate that required model deployments are accessible.

### Solution 4 — Validate before deployment

Test model availability in development and staging environments before deploying a new model configuration.

### Important distinction

| Provider outage | Model unavailability |
| --- | --- |
| Provider service is down | Specific model is inaccessible |
| Multiple models may fail | Other models may work |
| Provider fallback may help | Model fallback may be enough |

**Memory trick:**

> Provider is healthy, but your selected model is not available.

quiz.question: Why does Model Unavailability happen?
options: Incorrect routing conditions; Missing state values; Incorrect intent classification.
Too many user requests; Large prompts; Long responses.
Provider releases newer models; Older models become expensive to maintain; Provider changes infrastructure.

quiz.question: How to detect Model Unavailability?
options: Track: Daily token consumption; Monthly token consumption; Input/output token ratios.
Application failures with no corresponding logs; Missing timestamps; Logs from some agents but not others.
Monitor: Backup job success and failure; Backup age; Backup storage availability.
Model identifier; Provider model catalog; Region and deployment configuration.
quiz.explanation: Check: Model identifier. Provider model catalog. Region and deployment configuration.

options: Where supported, use JSON mode or schema-constrained output.
Store completed tasks and their results.
Generate unique request IDs; Propagate correlation IDs through service calls; Use OpenTelemetry trace context.
